evidence.claims: README rows for per-control, score and objective rules match the code; docs/SOURCES.md cites each rule; flagships.yaml entry now names ventures/cmmc (PR #19992 fix verified). The marketing FAQ said nothing about exceptions before this PR.

defects.what: Prior defect 0, open on arrival: enduring exceptions and temporary deficiencies, assessed MET by 32 CFR 170.24(b)(1)(i)-(ii), could not be recorded. Fixed in this PR: kind + description on an implemented Level 2 requirement, scored MET, listed in `exceptions`, printed in the SSP.

Control import hand-counted 7 bound values per inserted row; any new defaulted column (this PR's met_exception_detail made it 8) pushes a 14-row chunk past D1's 100 and returns a 500 on a full import. Fixed in this PR: counted from the table, test pins it.
An exception can be recorded on 3.12.4 (the SSP itself), which then counts MET with an objective not met, although the exception must be described in that SSP. Not refused yet; ROADMAP Next.
The 170.24(b)(1) and 170.4 wording is applied as the 2026-11-26 audit quoted it; no session has re-read it at eCFR and it is not in official-text.json. docs/SOURCES.md says so.

verdict: Meets the bar (correctness 3, claims 3, verification 3, median 3); finished (completeness 3); fitness 2 on arrival. All four low defects PR #19992 marked are closed (objective clearing tested, Level 1 copies pinned, flagships entry current, conflict guard's mutant now caught). The one medium left open, no way to record an enduring exception or a temporary deficiency under an operational plan of action, is fixed in PR #20112, scored here before the fix: a described exception on an implemented Level 2 requirement now scores MET (3.5.3 with [a] not met: 110, versus 105 with a blank description), the SSP prints it, Level 1 ignores it. Two lows remain: an exception is accepted on 3.12.4, and the rule text was not re-read at source (eCFR unreachable). Four hand-recomputed score cases and five seeded mutations, all caught.
